newsitem.title: UK: Frost sees more UK petrol station closures.
newsitem.headline: Frost sees more UK petrol station closures.

text.p: British petrol retailer Frost Group Plc said on Wednesday it expected more petrol stations to close in the UK fuels market as a bitter price war continues.
"There will be a further considerable number of site closures and also further rationalisation amongst the suppliers," chairman James Frost told shareholders at their annual meeting.
As for the company's own rationalisation plans, Frost, which will change its name into Save Group Plc from Thursday, said it was keeping its options open.
The company has already been approached to participate in various company combinations seeking an industry restructuring.

But Frost said it was not clear yet whether any of these combinations would produce value to its members. "When and if there is something which is in the best interest of members, I shall report it," he said.
Frost said the first half of this year saw several failed market attempts of price hikes, which on balance produced results for Frost which are about the same as a year ago.
"Shareholders should not expect half year results very different from those of last year," Frost said.

He added it was impossible to predict second half results, although warning profits in the short term may be "lower than our best expectations" as Frost won't be tempted to sacrifice long-term profits for short-term volumes.
"(The company) will continue to pursue a strategy of profit maximisation rather than that of volume maximisation which is pursued by many of our competitors," Frost said.
He described the UK fuels retail industry as in a state of flux, but with bright longer-term prospects.
"Whilst the pain will have lasted longer and has been deeper than could have been anticipated, the greater rewards will come and will come earlier," Frost said.
The ferocious price war in the British petrol market forced the closure of 1,500 or nearly 10 percent of all filling stations last year.
Shares in Frost Group dropped 27-1/2 pence to 92-1/2 at midday.
